title: GitOps with ArgoCD 🔄
description: Declare your cluster’s desired state in Git and let ArgoCD sync it automatically.

slides.title: What is GitOps? 🤔
slides.content:
# Git is the single source of truth

In GitOps, you store all Kubernetes manifests (or Helm charts, Kustomize overlays) in a Git repository. A controller inside the cluster continuously compares the **desired state** (Git) with the **actual state** (cluster) and reconciles them.

This brings:
- Audit trail (every change is a commit)
- Rollback via `git revert`
- Developer self‑service (create a PR to deploy)
- Increased security (no direct kubectl access needed)

slides.title: ArgoCD – The Kubernetes Operator 👑
slides.content:
## One of the most popular GitOps tools

ArgoCD:
- Automatically syncs applications from Git to the cluster.
- Provides a web UI and CLI.
- Supports plain YAML, Helm, Kustomize, and Jsonnet.
- Tracks drift – shows if someone manually changed a resource.
- Multi‑tenancy – manage multiple clusters from one instance.

It runs inside the cluster (a controller) and watches Git repositories.

slides.title: Installing ArgoCD 🛠️
slides.content:
## Quick setup

```bash
kubectl create namespace argocd
kubectl apply -n argocd -f https://raw.githubusercontent.com/argoproj/argo-cd/stable/manifests/install.yaml
```

Access the UI:
```bash
kubectl port-forward svc/argocd-server -n argocd 8080:443
```

Initial password:
```bash
kubectl -n argocd get secret argocd-initial-admin-secret -o jsonpath="{.data.password}" | base64 -d
```

quizData.question: How does ArgoCD authenticate initially?

options.text: Admin username and a generated password

quizData.explanation: ArgoCD creates a default admin user with a password stored in a Secret.

slides.title: Defining an Application 📝
slides.content:
## Tell ArgoCD what to sync

An **Application** resource defines:
- **Source**: Git repo URL, path, revision.
- **Destination**: cluster and namespace.
- **Sync policy**: automatic or manual, pruning, self‑heal.

```yaml
apiVersion: argoproj.io/v1alpha1
kind: Application
metadata:
  name: myapp
  namespace: argocd
spec:
  project: default
  source:
    repoURL: https://github.com/myorg/myapp-gitops.git
    targetRevision: HEAD
    path: kustomize/overlays/staging
  destination:
    server: https://kubernetes.default.svc
    namespace: staging
  syncPolicy:
    automated:
      prune: true
      selfHeal: true
```

With `automated: {prune:true, selfHeal:true}`, ArgoCD will delete resources removed from Git and fix any manual changes.

slides.title: Apply and Watch
slides.codeSnippet:
kubectl apply -f myapp.yaml
argocd app get myapp --refresh
argocd app sync myapp

quizData.question: True or False: ArgoCD with selfHeal enabled will revert manual changes made via kubectl.
quizData.explanation: selfHeal automatically brings the cluster back to the desired state from Git.

slides.title: Progressive Delivery with Argo Rollouts 🚦
slides.content:
## Canary and blue‑green made easy

Argo Rollouts is an extension that provides advanced deployment strategies:
- **Canary** – step‑by‑step traffic shifting.
- **Blue‑Green** – instant cutover.

It replaces the standard Deployment with a `Rollout` resource and integrates with Ingress controllers for traffic management.

```yaml
apiVersion: argoproj.io/v1alpha1
kind: Rollout
...
strategy:
  canary:
    steps:
    - setWeight: 20
    - pause: {duration: 60}
    - setWeight: 50
    - pause: {}
```

slides.title: Sealed Secrets & External Secrets 🔐
slides.content:
## GitOps needs secret handling

You can't store plain‑text secrets in Git. Solutions:
- **Sealed Secrets** – encrypt secrets with a cluster‑specific key; the SealedSecret controller decrypts them inside the cluster.
- **External Secrets Operator** – syncs secrets from external providers (Vault, AWS, GCP) into Kubernetes Secrets.

Both are GitOps‑friendly: encrypted or pointer‑only data in Git, actual secrets live outside.

slides.title: Pro Tip 🚀
slides.content:
## Use Kustomize or Helm with ArgoCD

ArgoCD natively supports both. Use Kustomize for environment‑specific overlays; Helm for complex apps with dependencies.
